cohort: The study included 1,355 delivery records from Jiblah Referral Hospital, Ibb, Yemen, between December 2021 and September 2024.
finding: The study revealed an alarmingly high Cesarean delivery rate of 48.3% at a rural Yemeni hospital, more than triple WHO recommendations, with distinct predictors for emergency and elective procedures.
mod_finding: Emergency Cesarean deliveries were primarily driven by acute complications like fetal distress and hypertension, while elective Cesarean deliveries were strongly associated with advanced maternal age and urban residence.
cross-section timing: Data collected from December 2021 to September 2024
